newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST-ING Q3 seen strongly higher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-ING Q3 seen strongly higher.

text.p: Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV's (ING) third-quarter results on Thursday are expected to confirm the profit slowdown the financial services group forecast in August but it will still deliver strong growth.

Analysts said the easing in profit momentum in the third quarter would be seen in the group's banking operations because of a strong comparison base a year earlier, while the insurance business would have continued to provide strong earnings.
Forecasts of net profit for the nine months to September 30 range between 2.32 billion and 2.35 billion guilders, up between 23 and 25 percent on 1.88 billion guilders a year earlier.
This puts the third-quarter result at between 810 million and 840 million guilders, a rise of between 16 and 20 percent on the same period in 1995.
When announcing its interim results, ING said second half profit growth would not match the 27.9 percent of the first half, when trading income soared amid buoyant markets.
"We're looking for strong growth, with the life operations spearheading the growth," said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Jeff Meys.
He sees third-quarter banking profits growing only seven percent, with insurance profits up 25-30 percent.
Meys said life insurance typically delivered stable returns for Dutch insurers, which usually had a strong presence in their home market, and the United States and emerging markets.
In non-life, he said hurricane damage in the Caribbean would have depressed results by only 25 million guilders in the third-quarter this year, compared with 60 million a year ago.
Andrew Goodwin of UBS said he expected a reduction in ING's third quarter profits from securities and currency trading.
"Some of the indications we're getting from other banks is that trading conditions became more difficult in the third quarter. That's a big swing factor for ING," he said.
He said the ING Barings investment banking unit's results would be below ING's expectations, partly due to difficult times in Asia and South America, where it suffered staff losses.
ING bought Barings in March 1995 after it collapsed from derivatives trading losses and now includes its results within the ING Barings division.
Van Meer James Capel analyst Ton Gietman said the strong third-quarter performance of Brady Bonds and other third-world third country debt would have helped ING.
"On balance it's still a healthy quarter but not as much as the full first half of the year," he said.
He said the steep Dutch yield curve would have continued to assist the core banking operations.
But ING had absorbed large costs in improving internal controls within Barings in the wake of its collapse.
Jean-Paul van Bavel of F van Lanschot Bankiers expected more strong growth from life insurance and a continued improvement from non-life after a slow first quarter.
He said interest and commission income would have boosted the banking results, with Barings making a slightly positive contribution net of financing costs for the first time.
-- Garry West, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
